podcast.title: Departure from The M.G.'s
podcast.body: Louis Steinberg was replaced by Duck Dunn in Booker T and the M.G.'s after the band had achieved several hits. Steinberg publicly claimed his removal was racially motivated due to him being black and Steve Cropper wanting another white man in the band. "Steinberg always claimed that the main reason he was dropped from the MG's was because he was black, and Steve Krupper wanted another white man."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Originator of "Green Onions" Title
podcast.body: Louis Steinberg is credited with suggesting the title "Green Onions" for the instrumental track by Booker T and the M.G.'s, thinking that onions were "the funkiest thing he could think of." "Louis Steinberg thought that onions were the funkiest thing he could think of, and so the track became green onions."

podcast.title: Recalled for Otis Redding Session
podcast.body: When Otis Redding was unexpectedly given a chance to record, Steve Cropper immediately ran out to call Louis Steinberg, who was already packing away his bass, back into the studio to play on the impromptu session. "Cropper ran out to get Louis Steinberg, who was packing his bass away, and talent to bring it back into the studio."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Session Player for Early Stax Hits
podcast.body: Louis Steinberg was a crucial bass player on many early Stax recordings, including Rufus and Carla Thomas's "Because I Love You," The Mar-Keys' "Last Night," The Triumphs' "Burnt Biscuit," and William Bell's "You Don't Miss Your Water." "Also in the studio was David Porter, a teenager who sang in a band with Bob Talley, the trumpet player on the session."
